messages:
maya: Quick design review — updated autoscale panel (min/max + budget guardrails + burst picker). wanted to surface a few interaction questions before dev handoff.

ethan: looking now. main thing i saw: the budget slider seems to silently clamp burst? is that intentional? :thinking_face: 

maya: yes — design intent was budget -> hard cap on monthly spend and burst uses remaining headroom. but we should make that relationship explicit in the UI.

ara: suggestion: show a tiny inline callout under the burst selector: "Burst uses remaining budget; may be limited when budget is low." small info icon with tooltip.

ethan: +1. also keyboard users: the burst picker should be a proper select with arrow nav, not just a range control. current prototype uses a custom widget that traps focus.

ux-research: accessibility note — contrast on the min/max labels falls just below AA when rendered at 12px. bump to 14px or increase weight. tested with VoiceOver: the SLO slider label isn't read consistently because we render percent with a visual suffix rather than an accessible label.

maya: good catch. i'll update copy to include an aria-label like: "SLO target percent (p95 latency threshold)".

sam: UX copy nit: "min capacity" and "max capacity" feel technical. what about "minimum GPUs" / "maximum GPUs"? clearer for customers skimming.

sophia: agree. and for the budget slider change label to "Monthly budget (USD)" and show a tooltip: "Estimated monthly spend based on current traffic and config."

ethan: edge case: what happens if min > max after editing both quickly? we should validate on blur, not only on submit, and show inline error: "Minimum cannot exceed maximum".

maya: yes — we'll run optimistic validation: highlight field in amber and show suggested fix button: "Set min = max".

ara: design question: SLO slider — current range 0-100 but we coerce to 99.9 for p99 style SLOs. we need to show precision (0.1) when the SLO type is p99/p95. maybe dynamic step sizing.

ux-research: and include a small example beneath: "For p99, 99.9 means fewer slow responses than 99.0." users repeatedly confused in tests.

maya: okay — dynamic steps per SLO type, example microcopy, and tooltip. also we'll add a contextual link to docs: /docs/autoscaling#slo-guidance

infra-bot: deploy preview generated: https://preview.redwood.com/pr-#234/autoscale-panel (snapshot at 1769994325) :deploy: 

sam: visual nit: the guardrail badge (red triangle) is pretty small on hi-dpi screens. make it 18px min and add text alternative: "Budget guardrail triggered" for screen readers.

ethan: behavior nit: when a customer toggles dedicated GPU pool selection, the estimated cost updates but we don't persist until save. suggest live update + "unsaved changes" pill.

maya: agree. we'll do live preview of estimate and show unsaved pill. speak to PM for analytics — we want to track toggles without saving as impression events.

ux-research: final accessibility items: ensure sliders support arrow step increments of 1 and page up/down for larger jumps; add focus outline visible at 3px; ensure all icons have text alternatives.

maya: action items: 1) update copy (min/max -> min/max GPUs, budget label, SLO tooltip) 2) add inline guardrail tooltip + larger badge + sr text 3) keyboard/focus fixes for burst selector and sliders 4) validation on blur and suggested-fix button 5) live cost preview + unsaved pill 6) doc link for SLOs. i'll ping design PR later today.

sophia: pinging product for prioritization: low-risk copy + a11y fixes should go to patch release, behavior changes (live preview) can be in next sprint.

maya: sounds good. thanks all :sparkles:

ethan: thanks — will open tickets for a11y + validation. :eyes:
